claims.text: Additional purchasing customers per 1,000 customers sent the Mens e-mail, versus no e-mail
claims.denominator: 267/21,307 (Mens E-Mail) minus 122/21,306 (No E-Mail)
claims.uncertainty: 95% interval, normal approximation: 5.00 to 8.61

claims.text: Relative lift in purchase rate, Mens e-mail versus no e-mail
claims.denominator: 267/21,307 (Mens E-Mail) minus 122/21,306 (No E-Mail)
claims.uncertainty: ratio of two small rates; use the absolute figure first

claims.text: Incremental spend per customer sent the Mens e-mail, versus no e-mail
claims.denominator: mean spend of 21,307 (Mens E-Mail) minus mean spend of 21,306 (No E-Mail)
claims.uncertainty: 95% interval, normal approximation: 0.49 to 1.05

claims.text: Sensitivity: incremental spend per customer sent the Mens e-mail after dropping the 25 largest purchases from each arm
claims.denominator: as the full-sample claim, minus the 25 largest purchases in each of the two arms
claims.uncertainty: point estimate falls 18% against the full sample; spend is heavy-tailed (maximum purchase 499 USD in both arms)

claims.text: Additional purchasing customers per 1,000 customers sent the Womens e-mail, versus no e-mail
claims.denominator: 189/21,387 (Womens E-Mail) minus 122/21,306 (No E-Mail)
claims.uncertainty: 95% interval, normal approximation: 1.50 to 4.72

claims.text: Relative lift in purchase rate, Womens e-mail versus no e-mail
claims.denominator: 189/21,387 (Womens E-Mail) minus 122/21,306 (No E-Mail)
claims.uncertainty: ratio of two small rates; use the absolute figure first

claims.text: Incremental spend per customer sent the Womens e-mail, versus no e-mail
claims.denominator: mean spend of 21,387 (Womens E-Mail) minus mean spend of 21,306 (No E-Mail)
claims.uncertainty: 95% interval, normal approximation: 0.17 to 0.68

claims.text: Sensitivity: incremental spend per customer sent the Womens e-mail after dropping the 25 largest purchases from each arm
claims.denominator: as the full-sample claim, minus the 25 largest purchases in each of the two arms
claims.uncertainty: point estimate falls 17% against the full sample; spend is heavy-tailed (maximum purchase 499 USD in both arms)

claims.text: Customers in train / validation / test
claims.denominator: 64,000 customers, seeded split stratified by arm

claims.text: Held-out: additional buyers per 1,000 when every customer gets the Mens e-mail
claims.denominator: 113/8,524 e-mailed minus 50/8,523 not e-mailed, over the whole held-out arms

claims.denominator: 77/8,556 e-mailed minus 50/8,523 not e-mailed, over the whole held-out arms

claims.text: Held-out, 25% contact cap, Mens e-mail: additional buyers per 1,000 contacted, model targeting

claims.uncertainty: 95% interval, customer bootstrap (2000 resamples): 2.80 to 17.18

claims.text: Held-out, 25% contact cap, Mens e-mail: additional buyers per 1,000 contacted, random contacts (expected value)

claims.text: Model targeting minus random contacts at the 25% cap (Mens e-mail)
claims.denominator: model: 43/2,159 e-mailed minus 21/2,122 not e-mailed, inside the selected held-out customers; random: 113/8,524 e-mailed minus 50/8,523 not e-mailed, over the whole held-out arms
claims.uncertainty: paired 95% interval, customer bootstrap (2000 resamples): -3.52 to 8.75; includes zero

claims.text: Model targeting minus the recency rule at the 25% cap (Mens e-mail)
claims.denominator: model: 43/2,159 e-mailed minus 21/2,122 not e-mailed, inside the selected held-out customers; rule: 40/2,122 e-mailed minus 22/2,147 not e-mailed, inside the selected held-out customers
claims.uncertainty: paired 95% interval, customer bootstrap (2000 resamples): -5.50 to 8.16; includes zero

claims.text: Model targeting minus the past-spend rule at the 25% cap (Mens e-mail); this rule was not the one chosen on validation

claims.uncertainty: paired 95% interval, customer bootstrap (2000 resamples): -6.97 to 3.92

claims.text: Pre-registered verdict on model targeting versus random and the primary rule

claims.uncertainty: stable only if both paired 95% intervals lie above zero
